issues.t: Twin-turbo V8 burns oil and smokes on startup
issues.sym: You have to add oil often, sometimes about a quart every 1,000 miles, with no visible leak. Blue smoke may puff from the exhaust after the car sits or idles, and low-oil warnings come up between services.
issues.why: The 4.4L twin-turbo V8 puts both turbochargers inside the V between the cylinder banks, so the engine runs very hot. That heat hardens the valve stem seals and other seals, letting oil into the cylinders. Earlier engines (2009-2012) were the worst and were covered by BMW's Customer Care Package and a class-action settlement.
issues.next: Track how much oil you add. If it's more than a quart every few thousand miles or you see blue smoke, get a leak-down and oil consumption test at a BMW specialist. Ask a dealer with your VIN whether any goodwill or settlement coverage still applies.

issues.t: Worn valve stem seals make the V8 burn oil
issues.sym: Blue-white smoke from the exhaust after idling or on startup, rising oil use and frequent low-oil warnings. Left alone, the oil can ruin the catalytic converters.
issues.why: The rubber valve stem seals on the 4.4L and 4.8L V8 harden with heat and age, usually past 80,000-100,000 miles, and let oil slip past the valves into the cylinders.
issues.next: Keep the oil topped up and check it at every fill-up. Have a BMW specialist confirm the cause; independent shops often have cheaper seal-replacement methods than a dealer.

issues.t: Plastic cooling parts crack and the engine overheats
issues.sym: Coolant smell, white crusty marks on the radiator, a sudden cloud of steam from under the hood, the temperature gauge climbing in traffic, or a low-coolant warning.
issues.why: The radiator tanks, expansion tank and water pump impeller are plastic and turn brittle with age. Early expansion tanks can split with no warning, and a worn viscous fan clutch can't pull enough air at idle, so the engine overheats when stopped.
issues.next: If you see steam or the gauge rises, pull over and shut the engine off right away; overheating can warp the aluminum heads. Have the radiator, expansion tank, water pump, thermostat and fan clutch checked and replaced as a set if they are original.

issues.t: Coolant leaks from the engine valley on the V8
issues.sym: Low-coolant warnings, coolant smell, steam from the back of the engine, or the heater blowing cool air, especially after a warm start.
issues.why: The plastic coolant pipes and thermostat housing under the intake manifold crack with heat and age, often before 100,000 miles. Because they sit in the valley of the V8, the intake must come off to fix them.
issues.next: Don't keep topping up and driving; low coolant can overheat the engine fast. Have a pressure test done, and replace the valley pan gasket at the same time since the intake is already off.

issues.t: Coolant leaks and overheating on the twin-turbo V8
issues.sym: Low-coolant or engine-temperature warnings, a sweet coolant smell after driving, coolant puddles, or the car going into reduced-power mode.
issues.why: Heat from the turbos inside the V wears out the coolant hoses, turbo coolant lines, thermostat and expansion tank faster than on most engines.
issues.next: Check the coolant level often and act on the first warning. Stop driving if it overheats. Many specialists replace the thermostat and expansion tank as a precaution around 80,000-100,000 miles.

issues.t: Air suspension sags or the car sits low
issues.sym: One corner or the whole rear drops after the car is parked, the car sits on the ground in the morning, a suspension warning shows, or the compressor runs for a long time.
issues.why: The rubber air springs crack with age and leak, and the compressor wears out from running too much. The 2016-2022 cars saw many early air strut failures.
issues.next: Don't drive a car that is sitting very low; tires and body parts can be damaged. Have the system checked for leaks. For 2016-2022 cars, ask a dealer about BMW's extended coverage on the air struts.

issues.t: Valve cover and oil filter housing gaskets leak oil
issues.sym: Burning-oil smell after driving, light smoke from the engine bay, oil spots under the car, or oil-soaked belts.
issues.why: Rubber gaskets on the valve covers, oil filter housing, oil pan, alternator bracket and timing cover harden with heat and age, usually starting between 50,000 and 100,000 miles.
issues.next: Have the leak traced to its source. Fix it before oil drips onto the exhaust or soaks the drive belt, which can slip off and get pulled into the engine.

issues.t: Automatic transmission shifts harshly or slips
issues.sym: Delayed or harsh shifts, slipping, a transmission warning, the car refusing to shift out of Park, or going into a limp-home mode.
issues.why: The 6-speed automatic's mechatronic (valve body) unit and its sealing sleeve wear and leak, causing low pressure and erratic shifting. Long fluid-change intervals make it worse.
issues.next: Have the codes and fluid checked by a BMW specialist. Replacing the sealing sleeve, filter pan and fluid fixes many cars; a failed mechatronic unit or rebuild costs much more.

issues.t: Timing chain guides break on the V8
issues.sym: A rattle from the front of the engine, loudest on cold starts. Plastic pieces may show up when the oil is drained.
issues.why: The plastic upper timing chain guides turn brittle with heat and age, crack and break apart, and a worn tensioner lets the chain slap. If ignored, the chain can jump and wreck the engine.
issues.next: Don't ignore a cold-start rattle. Have the guides and tensioner inspected. If there's no record of the job by 80,000-100,000 miles, plan for it.

issues.t: VANOS valve timing seals wear and power drops
issues.sym: Rough idle, hesitation, a dip in mid-range power and a rattle on cold starts.
issues.why: The 1999-2001 version of the 4.4L V8 added VANOS variable valve timing on the intake camshafts. Its internal seals wear, so the system can't adjust timing properly.
issues.next: Have a BMW specialist check VANOS function and codes. New seals or a rebuilt VANOS unit usually fixes it.

issues.t: Valve cover leak floods spark plug wells and causes misfires
issues.sym: Misfires, a shaking idle, a flashing check engine light, or oil smell from the top of the engine.
issues.why: A small valve cover gasket leak lets oil pool in the spark plug wells, where it damages the short boots on the ignition coils.
issues.next: Have the valve cover gaskets and spark plug tube seals replaced, and replace any oil-damaged coils or boots.

issues.t: Crankcase vent valve fails and the engine idles rough
issues.sym: Erratic idle, extra exhaust smoke, oil leaks or a whistling sound from the engine.
issues.why: The crankcase ventilation (PCV) valve on the back of the intake manifold has a rubber diaphragm that tears with age. Crankcase pressure then rises and the engine pulls in extra air and oil.
issues.next: Have the vent valve and its hoses checked. It's a fairly cheap fix that can stop oil leaks and smoking.

issues.t: V12 cooling system leaks and overheats
issues.sym: Rising temperature gauge, coolant smell, low-coolant warning or coolant drips.
issues.why: The 5.4L V12 has two thermostats and two coolant circuits, so there are many more aging hoses and parts that can leak or fail.
issues.next: Treat any coolant loss as urgent and have the whole cooling system pressure-tested. Labor is high because the V12 fills the engine bay.

issues.t: Front thrust arm bushings wear and the wheel shimmies when braking
issues.sym: The steering wheel shakes or wobbles under braking, often around 50-60 mph, with wandering or vague steering.
issues.why: The rubber bushings in the front thrust arms (also called tension struts) wear out, letting the front wheels move under braking.
issues.next: Have the front suspension inspected. New thrust arms or bushings usually cure it; check that the brake rotors aren't warped too.

issues.t: ABS and traction control module fails when hot
issues.sym: The ABS, traction control and brake warning lights come on, usually once the car is warm, and go out after it cools. ABS doesn't work while the lights are on.
issues.why: The electronic control unit attached to the ABS pump develops internal faults that show up with heat.
issues.next: Normal braking still works, but without ABS. Have the codes read; the control unit can often be repaired or rebuilt rather than replaced.

issues.t: Fuel injectors fail on the V12
issues.sym: Misfires, rough running, a check engine light or hard starting.
issues.why: The 6.0L V12's direct fuel injectors wear and stop delivering fuel evenly, usually from about 70,000 miles.
issues.next: Have the misfire codes read and the injectors tested. Fix it soon, since misfires can damage the catalytic converters.

issues.t: Car Access System fault stops the car from starting
issues.sym: The car won't start or crank, the key isn't recognized, or start problems come and go.
issues.why: The Car Access System (CAS) module, which checks the key and allows starting, can fail. It is more common on the early cars before the 2006 update.
issues.next: Have a BMW specialist read the module codes before replacing parts. A new module must be programmed to the car and keys.

issues.t: Soft-close doors can look shut but open while driving (recall)
issues.sym: A door-ajar warning that comes and goes, or a door that doesn't pull itself fully closed.
issues.why: On cars with Comfort Access and soft-close doors, a door can appear latched when it isn't and may open while driving. BMW recalled 2005-2007 cars in 2012 and widened it to 2005-2008 in 2017.
issues.next: Have a BMW dealer check that both recall repairs are done. Until then, close each door firmly and watch the door-ajar warning.

issues.t: Car can roll away if left in Neutral instead of Park (recall)
issues.sym: After shutting the car off, the gear display doesn't show P.
issues.why: On cars with Comfort Access, pressing the Start/Stop button two or three times quickly can leave the electronic transmission in Neutral instead of Park, so the car can roll if the parking brake isn't set.
issues.next: Always set the parking brake and check that P shows before leaving. Have a BMW dealer confirm the software update is done.

issues.t: Brake vacuum pump valve can leak oil and weaken the brakes (recall)
issues.sym: A harder brake pedal that needs more force, or longer stopping distances.
issues.why: A check valve on the brake vacuum pump can leak engine oil into the brake booster, reducing or, in rare cases, eliminating power braking assist.
issues.next: If the pedal feels hard, have it checked right away. Ask a BMW dealer whether the recall work is done on your car.

issues.t: Ignition coils and spark plugs cause misfires on the V12
issues.sym: Rough running, a shaking idle, a flashing check engine light or loss of power.
issues.why: The twin-turbo V12's coils and plugs wear out, and reaching all 12 cylinders takes a lot of labor.
issues.next: Have the misfire codes read. Replace worn plugs and any failed coils; many owners replace all coils at once.

issues.t: Turbo cooling pump circuit board can overheat (recall)
issues.sym: A burning smell after shutting the car off, or coolant and engine-overheating warnings.
issues.why: The circuit board in the electric auxiliary water pump that cools the turbochargers can overheat and smolder, which could start a fire in the engine bay. BMW recalled it in 2011-2012 and again in 2018 for cars whose pumps could still fail.
issues.next: Check your VIN for all the auxiliary pump recalls. If one is open, park outside until the pump is replaced.

issues.t: Fuel injectors or high-pressure pump fail and the engine misfires
issues.sym: Rough idle, misfires, hesitation, loss of power, stalling, a check engine light or a Drivetrain Malfunction warning.
issues.why: The direct-injection turbo engines are hard on their high-pressure fuel pumps and injectors. The 2011-2012 740i (N54) and the twin-turbo V8 are known for it. BMW extended warranty coverage on some of these parts to 10 years or 120,000 miles.
issues.next: Have the fuel pressure and injector codes checked by a BMW specialist. Ask a dealer whether extended warranty coverage applies to your VIN.

issues.t: Plastic turbo charge pipe cracks and power drops
issues.sym: A sudden loss of power, a loud pop or hissing under hard acceleration, and a check engine light.
issues.why: The plastic pipe that carries pressurized air from the turbo toward the intercooler cracks under boost pressure on the 3.0L turbo six.
issues.next: The car is usually drivable gently but slow. Have the pipe replaced; many owners fit a stronger aluminum pipe.

issues.t: Airbag control module can reset (recall)
issues.sym: The airbag warning light comes on now and then.
issues.why: Metal particles left from manufacturing can short the airbag control module on early 2016 cars and make it reset. If a crash happens during a reset, the airbags may not deploy.
issues.next: If the airbag light is on, have the car checked right away. Confirm with a BMW dealer that the module replacement was done.

issues.t: Active grille shutters stick and turn on the check engine light
issues.sym: Check engine light, sometimes with code P05A0, and grille flaps stuck open or closed.
issues.why: The motor-driven shutters behind the grille that open and close to control airflow fail or jam.
issues.next: This isn't urgent, but have it fixed so the light doesn't hide other problems. Ask a BMW dealer about the extended coverage on these parts.

issues.t: Thermostat housing cracks and leaks coolant
issues.sym: Low-coolant warning, coolant smell or drips, and in time rising engine temperature.
issues.why: The plastic thermostat housing on the 3.0L turbo six cracks with age, usually after about 80,000 miles.
issues.next: Have the leak confirmed and the housing replaced before the engine overheats.

issues.t: V12 valve cover and injector seals leak
issues.sym: Burning-oil smell, oil around the top of the engine, or misfires.
issues.why: On the M760i's twin-turbo V12, valve cover gaskets and fuel injector seals wear from heat, usually around 50,000-70,000 miles.
issues.next: Have the leaks traced and fixed together where possible, since access on the V12 takes a lot of labor.

issues.t: Plug-in hybrid battery loses range or shows charging errors
issues.sym: Shorter electric-only range, hybrid system or charging warnings, or the car refusing to charge.
issues.why: The high-voltage battery loses capacity with age and mileage, and the electric drive and charging modules can throw faults. Some are fixed with software, others need parts.
issues.next: Have a BMW dealer read the hybrid codes and check for software updates first. The high-voltage battery has its own longer warranty, so check its terms before paying.

issues.t: Integrated brake unit can lose power assist and ABS (recall)
issues.sym: Brake or stability-control warnings, a hard brake pedal or longer stopping distances.
issues.why: The supplier-built integrated braking system can fail, cutting power brake assist and switching off ABS and stability control. BMW has issued several recalls (24V-104, 24V-697, 24V-739 and 26V-422); cars fixed under the earlier ones need the newer fix.
issues.next: If a brake warning comes on, drive gently to a dealer or have the car towed. Check your VIN for every brake recall.

issues.t: Steering shaft joint can break (recall)
issues.sym: Steering suddenly takes much more effort.
issues.why: A joint in the steering spindle (shaft) can break on certain 2024-2025 cars.
issues.next: If steering suddenly feels heavy, pull over safely and have the car towed. Have the dealer replace the joint under the recall.

issues.t: Hands-on steering wheel sensor can stop working (recall)
issues.sym: Driver-assist features that need hands on the wheel may not recognize your hands, or warnings about the system may appear.
issues.why: A ground connection in the steering wheel may be loose, which can disable hands-on detection and keep the emergency stop assistant from working.
issues.next: Have a BMW dealer inspect and reattach the connection.

issues.t: A/C wiring can be damaged during a cabin filter change (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning. A burning smell or electrical faults after a cabin air filter change could be a sign.
issues.why: A screw on the cabin air filter housing cover can pinch the air conditioning wiring harness when the filter is replaced, which could short and start a fire.
issues.next: Park outside until the recall is done. Have the dealer inspect the harness and add the retaining strap.

issues.t: i7 high-voltage system can shut down and lose drive power (recall)
issues.sym: A sudden loss of drive power with electric drive warnings.
issues.why: Software in the i7's motor controller can shut down the high-voltage system. A separate recall covers battery modules that may be assembled wrong and could fail or catch fire.
issues.next: Make sure the over-the-air or dealer software update is installed, and check your VIN for the battery module recall too.

issues.t: 750e driveshaft connection can fail (recall)
issues.sym: Loss of power to the rear wheels, or the car rolling if parked without the parking brake.
issues.why: The joint between the driveshaft and the rear differential may be damaged on the 750e plug-in hybrid.
issues.next: Always set the parking brake. Have the dealer inspect the joint and repair or replace parts under the recall.
